figures.name: rumour_curves
figures.caption: Diffusion in each of the 250 seeded branches: cumulative share of agents who saw the rumour (the seed post, or a repost or quote of it) in a feed, and who engaged with it (like, comment, repost, quote, or follow of the poster), by step. Blue: seeded by one of the 36 core users; orange: by a regular user. Black: median over branches. The two branches with the widest reach are labelled by seed agent.

figures.name: rumour_followers
figures.caption: Reach by step 16 against the seed agent's follower count at the fork (regular users follow only core users, so every regular user has 0 followers; small horizontal jitter added). Spearman correlation of followers with reach 0.61 over all seeds, but only 0.45 among the 36 core users: being a core user matters more than how many followers it has. Regular seeders fall into two groups (see the next figure).

figures.name: rumour_top
figures.caption: Ranking of seed agents by how many agents saw their rumour by step 16; the label gives agents reached, agents who engaged, reposts and quotes of the seed post, and the step at which 10% of agents had seen it. The best regular seeder ranks 36.

figures.name: rumour_hub
figures.caption: Reach is decided mostly by whether core user 22 reposts the rumour at step 7, the first step after it is posted. That happened in 179 of 250 branches. Among regular seeders (no followers), the branches split into two tight groups: 12-14 agents reached without that repost, and 31-35 with it. In every regular branch the post has the same id and is shown at step 7 to the same two agents (22 and 199) by the recommender's random slots. Agent 22's prompt differs between branches only in the post's author id, and its sampling seed is the same; it always comments, and reposts in 150 of 214. So the split reflects one sampled decision that flips on the author's id number, not anything about the seeder. Lines: median; bands: min-max over the branches in each group.
